title: Question 11
stem:
Some of the electron energy bands in a solid are illustrated in Fig. 11.1.

{{figure:figure_11_1}}

Fig. 11.1

The width of the forbidden band and the number of charge carriers occupying each band depends on the nature of the solid.
Use band theory to explain why the resistance of a sample of a metal at room temperature changes with increasing temperature.

parts.text: Use band theory to explain why the resistance of a sample of a metal at room temperature changes with increasing temperature.

markscheme_points.text: in a metal, conduction band overlaps valence band / there is no forbidden band
as temperature rises, there is no significant increase in the number of free electrons / charge carriers
as temperature rises, lattice ion vibrations increase in amplitude
increased lattice vibrations restrict the movement of electrons / increase scattering of charge carriers
drift velocity / current decreases, so electrical resistance increases

hints: Hint 1: In a metal, the conduction band overlaps the valence band, providing a large and fixed concentration of free electrons.
Hint 2: Consider whether heating adds significantly to the existing large sea of conduction electrons.
Hint 3: Consider how temperature affects the vibrating positive lattice ions and electron mean free path.
Hint 4: Connect the increased rate of electron-lattice collisions to the change in drift velocity and macroscopic resistance.
Hint 5: State clearly the final conclusion that the electrical resistance of the metal increases with increasing temperature.
parts.proper_answer: Conduction band overlaps valence band with plentiful free electrons. As temperature rises, lattice vibrations increase, restricting electron movement so resistance increases.
walkthrough:
Step 1: **Identify Governing Principle**
In metals, the conduction band overlaps with the valence band, so no energy gap exists and free charge carriers are already abundant at room temperature.

Step 2: **Analyze Carrier Density vs Lattice Scattering**
Unlike semiconductors, raising temperature does not increase the carrier concentration because the conduction band is already partially filled. However, thermal energy increases the amplitude of vibration of the positive lattice ions.

Step 3: **Conclusion on Resistance**
The increased lattice vibrations scatter conducting electrons more frequently, reducing their drift velocity. Consequently, current for a given p.d. decreases and electrical resistance increases.
